title: Loams connector manifest (loams.flow/v1 Connector)
description: One versioned manifest per connector, at connectors/registry/<id>.yaml, loaded at start and served by FlowService.ListConnectors/DescribeConnector (design §33 D352). Every connector declares its capabilities — direction, modes, delivery, transactional and upsert/delete support, ordering, formats, schema handling, bulk Arrow support, backpressure, auth methods, config schema, secret fields and limits — and ValidateRoute refuses a route that uses an undeclared one (design §33 D353, §4 rule 1). A capability removed or narrowed bumps specVersion's major (§33 §4 rule 4). CN1 Task 1 owns this file; the protobuf mirror is fabric/proto/loams/flow/v1/connector.proto, the YAML is the source and CI checks that the two agree (§33 §4, last paragraph).

apiVersion.description: The manifest's API version. Constant in CN1: the only shape is loams.flow/v1 (design §33 §4).

kind.description: The manifest's kind. Constant in CN1: the only shape is Connector (design §33 §4).

id.description: The connector's registry key, unique across the registry; matches the file name connectors/registry/<id>.yaml (design §33 §4, D352).

name.description: The connector's display name, for example "Apache Kafka" (design §33 §4).

specVersion.description: The version of this manifest, not of the connector; bumps on every capability change, and a removal or narrowing bumps the major (§33 §4 rule 4). Semver, kept as a string so the manifest needs no semver library to read; loams-flow parses it (CN1 Task 1).

category.description: The kind of system the connector speaks to (§33 §4's category comment; the registry is grouped by it).

priority.description: The rollout phase: P1 is the ★ set of CN1, P2 is CN2, P3 is CN3's long tail through OpenAPI-generated connectors (§33 §8, D358). CN2's owner rulings make P1 and P2 first-party native by default, with Camel, Debezium Server and Iggy plugins only as declared fallbacks (CN2 OR-1, OR-4; rule R-CN2-6).

starred.description: True for the 21 ★ connectors Loams owns and ships in CN1 (§33 §8, D358). CN1's semantic rules imply priority = P1 from starred.

status.description: The connector's maturity. "planned" is a generated stub with no capability detail yet (CN1 Ruling 1); "deprecated" keeps its major so routes pinned to it keep running (§33 §4 rule 4).

runtime.description: Which runtime runs this connector (design §33 §5, D354): native Rust on the connector SDK, Iggy's connectors runtime, unmodified Camel in loams-connect, Debezium Server, or a native connector generated from an OpenAPI spec. kind and ref are the default for both directions; source and sink override them per direction (CN2 OR-10), profile names a target or HTTP-API profile, and fallback declares the one non-default runtime an instance may opt into (CN2 OR-4).

kind.description: The runtime (§33 §5, D354). A connector exists once per runtime it is shipped as; the manifest describes the runtime Loams ships (§33 §4 rule 2).

ref.description: What the runtime points at, per kind: a crate path (loams_flow::connectors::kafka), an Iggy plugin name, a Camel URI scheme, a Debezium connector class, or an OpenAPI spec URL (§33 §4's runtime.ref comment).

version.description: The pinned driver or library version behind ref, free-form because it spans crates and native builds, for example "rdkafka 0.39 / librdkafka 2.x (verify)" (§33 §4).

source.description: Overrides kind and ref for the source direction (CN2 OR-10). Only on a manifest that declares capabilities.source (R-CN2-1).

sink.description: Overrides kind and ref for the sink direction (CN2 OR-10). Only on a manifest that declares capabilities.sink (R-CN2-1).

profile.description: A profile id under connectors/profiles/<id>.yaml: a target profile (a protocol-compatible system served by a family module, CN2 OR-2) or an HTTP-API profile (CN2 OR-11). Set only when every declared direction runs native by default, and the file must exist (R-CN2-2). null or absent when there is none.

fallback.description: The declared, temporary fallback runtime (CN2 OR-4): never the default, an instance opts in with runtime: fallback. Camel, Debezium or Iggy only, in declared directions, naming the task that made it a fallback or replaces it (R-CN2-8).

licence.description: The licences the gate checks: the runtime component's own, and every library or driver it loads (design §33 D359). CI refuses AGPL, BSL, SSPL, ELv2, NOASSERTION and unknown ids for anything in the image; a SaaS service used through its public API is not a licence question, so its dependencies may be empty.

component.description: An SPDX id for the runtime component, for example "Apache-2.0" (design §33 D359).

dependencies.description: Every library or driver the connector loads, by name, with its SPDX id (design §33 D359). Optional, because a component with no loaded dependency declares none.

additionalProperties.description: An SPDX id for one loaded dependency.

capabilities.description: What the connector can do, declared rather than inferred (design §33 D353). delivery, ordering, formats, schema, bulk and backpressure are required of every connector; source and sink are optional, because a connector may be one direction only (a webhook source, a JDBC sink), and which of the two is present says which. A route that uses an undeclared capability is refused by name, capability and manifest version (§33 §4 rule 1).

source.description: What the connector does as a source. Omit for a sink-only connector.

cdc.description: Row-level change capture (design §33 §7, D357). CN1's semantic rules require source.streaming and a non-empty position when this is true.

webhook.description: Receives webhooks as a source (CN1 Task 4's HMAC, GitHub, Stripe, Slack and Shopify schemes).

resumable.description: Restarts from a committed position, which is what makes an at-least-once source safe to kill and restart (CN1 Ruling 4).

position.description: What the source checkpoints, for example "kafka-offsets" (§33 §4). Free-form, because each system names its own position; empty when the source has none.

sink.description: What the connector does as a sink. Omit for a source-only connector.

transactional.description: The sink writes inside the target system's transaction and stores Loams' checkpoint atomically with the data (TransactionalSink). delivery.sink may be exactly_once only when this is true (CN2 OR-7, R-CN2-7).

upsert.description: The sink upserts by a key it declares in its config schema. A route that upserts needs this (§33 §4 rule 1).

delete.description: The sink applies deletes, which a CDC route needs.

idempotent.description: The sink itself dedupes retries, for example Kafka's idempotent producer. With upsert, this is what lets delivery.sink be effectively_once (CN2 OR-7, R-CN2-7).

reply.description: The sink emits one reply event per input event to a declared reply topic (CN2 OR-19: AI and function connectors). Requires a non-empty envelope.emits and a reply_topic property in the config schema (R-CN2-3). false when omitted.

delivery.description: The delivery guarantee per direction. At-least-once is the floor (§33 §6); effectively_once is declared where the target dedupes by ce_id or a natural key, or a source's ids are stable across re-reads; exactly_once only through a TransactionalSink (CN2 OR-7, R-CN2-7).

source.description: The source's guarantee: re-delivery after a crash is expected. effectively_once requires envelope.stable_ids (CN2 OR-7, R-CN2-7).

sink.description: The sink's guarantee. exactly_once requires sink.transactional and the exactly-once suite; effectively_once requires sink.idempotent or sink.upsert (CN2 OR-7, R-CN2-7).

ordering.description: The order events keep. A route that relies on per-partition order needs at least per_partition here (§33 §4 rule 1).

formats.description: The wire and payload formats the connector emits or consumes (§33 §4). CloudEvents is the envelope for everything else (D355), and Avro appears only at Kafka and schema-registry boundaries (D356).

schema.description: Schema handling: whether a schema registry is involved, and how the connector evolves a schema on it (§33 §4).

registry.description: Whether the connector needs a schema registry. Avro at a registry boundary is the only registry-shaped case (D356).

evolution.description: The compatibility rule the connector holds its schemas to (§33 §4).

bulk.description: Bulk path. Bulk data moves as Arrow, never row by row (design §33 D356); max_batch_rows is the batch size CN1 Ruling 3 defaults to 65536.

arrow.description: The connector takes or produces Arrow IPC batches (design §33 D356).

max_batch_rows.description: Rows per Arrow batch; at least 1, 65536 by default (CN1 Ruling 3).

backpressure.description: How the sink tells the Fabric to slow down (§33 §4).

auth.description: The auth methods the connector accepts, as the slugs of §33 Appendix A's legend. CN1's semantic rules require every value to be one of them; secrets for these are named in secrets and resolved through the namespace's secret store (D189), never stored in the instance.

config.description: Where the connector's instance-config JSON Schema lives. The manifest declares the shape of an instance's settings (design §33 D353); it does not inline them, so one schema serves every instance of the connector.

$ref.description: A repository-relative path to the connector's instance-config JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) under connectors/, for example schemas/kafka.config.json. Resolved and applied by loams-flow at load time; CI checks that the file exists, so a manifest cannot point at a schema that is not there.

secrets.description: The config fields that hold secrets, named. Resolved through the namespace's secret store (D189) and never stored in the instance; CN1's semantic rules require every name to appear in the config schema with "writeOnly": true.

items.description: One config field's name, for example "sasl.password".

envelope.description: The CloudEvents contract this connector emits and consumes (design §33 D355): one CloudEvent per record, row change or file, with type io.loams.dev.flow.<connector>.<event>.v1 and source /connectors/<instance>/<resource>.

emits.description: The CloudEvents type this connector emits, for example io.loams.dev.flow.kafka.record.v1, or "" when it emits none (a sink-only connector). Never "*": an emitted type is concrete.

consumes.description: The CloudEvents type this connector consumes, or "*" for any type (§33 §4's kafka example, which sinks to any topic).

passthrough.description: Input that already is a valid CloudEvent keeps its producer's type, source and id, and the connector adds only the loamsconnector and loamsinstance extensions (§33 §6). A manifest that passes events through declares this, and its contract test checks both the pass-through and the wrapped case.

stable_ids.description: The source's CloudEvents ids are stable across re-reads, so ingest's (source, id) dedup (D334) makes it effectively once (§33 §6, CN2 OR-7). false when omitted.

limits.description: The bounds the runtime enforces on this connector's records and batches (§33 §4). An omitted bound leaves the runtime's default; batch_bytes defaults to 8 MiB (CN1 Ruling 3, Iggy's message size limit).

max_record_bytes.description: The largest single record the connector accepts or emits, in bytes; at least 1.

batch_rows.description: Rows per batch for a batch connector, at least 1; the Arrow default is 65536 (CN1 Ruling 3).

batch_bytes.description: The largest batch the connector sends, in bytes, at least 1; Ruling 3's default is 8 MiB.

conformance.description: The suites the connector passes (§33 §4 rule 3): contract exercises each declared capability, roundtrip sends sink → source and reads the events back, kill-restart kills the runtime mid-batch, dup-check bounds duplicates by the declared delivery, bulk runs the Arrow path at 1 M rows, cdc exercises inserts, updates, deletes, DDL and slot or binlog resume; CN2 adds schema-evolution, backpressure, exactly-once (a crash at every fault point of the two-phase write) and auth (CN2 Task 6). status preview or stable requires contract (R-CN2-5).

notes.description: Free-form notes about the manifest (CN2 Task 1). Conventional prefixes: "narrows: …" for a capability a target lacks, "fallback-only: …" for a P1 or P2 direction whose default runtime is not native, naming one of CN2 OR-4's reasons (R-CN2-6), and "java-deferred: …". Empty when omitted.

docs.description: A repository-relative path to the connector's guide page; null when it has none. Optional because a generated stub has none (CN1 Ruling 1).

delivery.description: One direction's delivery guarantee (§33 §4's capabilities.delivery, D355; effectively_once is CN2 OR-7's, appended so the protobuf numbering keeps declaration order).

direction.description: One direction of a connector, as capabilities names it.

runtimeOverride.description: One direction's runtime, overriding runtime.kind and runtime.ref (CN2 OR-10).

kind.description: The runtime for this direction; runtime.kind's enum.

ref.description: What the runtime points at for this direction, with runtime.ref's per-kind meaning.

kind.description: The fallback runtime: camel, debezium or iggy (R-CN2-8). Typed with runtime.kind's enum so the semantic rule, not the schema, names the refusal.

ref.description: What the fallback runtime points at, with runtime.ref's per-kind meaning.

directions.description: The directions the fallback serves; each must be declared under capabilities (R-CN2-8).

replaced_by.description: The task that made this a fallback, or "CN2 Task 23" for the replacement queue. Non-empty (R-CN2-8).
